title: S021 — Incremental support aggregate / fixpoint primitive
description: Determine whether support evaluation can be represented as an incrementally maintained aggregate so that a local judgment change updates support state without re-evaluating the entire support expression.
result_summary: HOLD. The support expression CAN be represented as a compact, EXACT, locally updatable aggregate. The reference conjoin/disjoin are commutative/associative lattice meets over the member multiset, so a per-group count is a sufficient statistic: group {n, nTrue, nFalseOrBoth} -> conjoin; node group-result vector -> disjoin. Measured: 667 conjunctive groups with 0 aggregate mismatches, 635 disjunctive nodes with 0 mismatches, and 6 incremental member-flip updates with 0 mismatches against full recomputation (O(1) per member change). No second causal engine: the aggregate re-expresses the SAME lattice meet over a sufficient statistic. BOUNDARY: Phase B (unfoundedSet) is a GLOBAL candidate-set fixpoint, not a per-group aggregate, so it must remain a separate global consistency stage; topology changes alter group SHAPE (structural update). HOLD because the cycle/unfounded and topology boundaries were characterised but not tested, and the aggregate is a primitive, not yet an engine.

answers.Q3_min_info_four: counts of TRUE / FALSE-or-BOTH / NEITHER per group (NEITHER is the residual) plus the group-result vector
answers.Q5_support_switching: YES - the group-result vector IS the switching state; no full derivation needed
answers.Q6_shared_support: YES - shared members update each consuming group independently
answers.Q7_where_it_stops: the cycle/unfounded boundary: Phase B is a global candidate-set fixpoint, not a per-group aggregate
answers.Q8_cycle_separate_barrier: YES - unfounded/cycle reasoning can remain a separate global consistency barrier
answers.Q9_explains_s020: partially - the aggregate identifies when a previous support is no longer valid, but not the downstream consequence
answers.Q10_future_state: per-group counts, the group-result vector, the member->group index, plus (separately) the negated/forcedBy accumulators and a global Phase B barrier

next_experiment: test the aggregate against cycle/unfounded and topology-change cases, then design an execution strategy that pairs the aggregate with the global Phase B barrier.
limitations: Cycle/unfounded and topology-change cases were characterised, not tested (budget).
The incremental update test exercised only 6 member-flips on one sampled model.
Branch isolation and determinism not separately measured.
